unit.can_do_en: ask the way and follow left, right and straight on.

brief.situation_en: Maria asks Pasi on the street.

lines.speaker: Maria
lines.gloss_en: Excuse me, how do I get to the Ateneum?

judge.reason: Only register differences (anteeks/anteeksi, mä/minä); same question.
Mee/mene and katuu/katua are spoken variants; same instruction.

lines.speaker: Pasi
lines.text_puhe: Toiseen risteykseen asti. Sit käänny vasemmalle.
lines.text_kirja: Toiseen risteykseen asti. Sitten käänny vasemmalle.
lines.gloss_en: To the second crossing. Then turn left.

judge.reason: Sit/sitten only differs in register; same directions.

puhe.text: Toiseen risteykseen asti. Sit käänny vasemmalle.

kirja.text: Toiseen risteykseen asti. Sitten käänny vasemmalle.

judge.reason: Okei/selvä are both acknowledgments; sit/sitten is register only.

lines.speaker: Pasi
lines.text_puhe: Ateneum on oikeel puolel, rautatieaseman vieres.
lines.text_kirja: Ateneum on oikealla puolella, rautatieaseman vieressä.
lines.gloss_en: The Ateneum is on the right, next to the railway station.

judge.reason: Spoken oikeel puolel, vieres equal written oikealla puolella, vieressä; same location.

puhe.text: Ateneum on oikeel puolel, rautatieaseman vieres.

kirja.text: Ateneum on oikealla puolella, rautatieaseman vieressä.

judge.reason: Onks/onko is register only; same question.
Minuuttii/minuuttia is a spoken variant; same number and meaning.

forms.why_en: Speech drops the final i: anteeksi becomes anteeks.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Speech shortens minä to mä. Books write minä.
Päästä, to get somewhere, with -n for 'I': pääsen.
Mennä without its ending tells someone to go: mene. Speech says mee.
Suora, straight, with -an: suoraan, straight ahead.
The partitive singular of tämä after 'en ymmärrä': tätä.
Moving along a street takes -a: katu becomes katua. Speech turns -ua into -uu.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Adds -lle for 'to' a point: pitkä, 'long', becomes pitkälle, 'how far'.
Adds -en for 'to': toinen becomes toiseen, to match risteykseen.
Adds -en for 'to': risteys becomes risteykseen.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Speech shortens sitten to sit. Books write sitten.
Kääntyä, to turn. To tell one person to turn, use käänny: the nt becomes nn.
Adds -lle for direction: vasen becomes vasemmalle, 'to the left'.
Okei is the everyday spoken OK. Books write selvä, which means clear.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
The form of olla, to be, for he, she or it. People say it the same way.
Adds -lla for 'on': oikea becomes oikealla. Speech says oikeel.
Adds -lla for 'on': puoli becomes puolella. Speech shortens -lla to -l: puolella becomes puolel.
Vieressä, 'next to', needs -n on the word before: rautatieasema becomes rautatieaseman.
Vieressä means next to and comes after its word. Speech shortens -ssä to -s: Vieressä becomes Vieres.

forms.form_name_en: present tense, 3rd person singular, with the question ending -ko/-kö
forms.why_en: On with -ko to ask a question. Speech often says -ks: onks.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
Kaukana means far away, at a distance.
Ei on its own answers 'no'. People say it the same way.
This is the dictionary form. People say it the same way.
After a number the noun takes the partitive: kymmenen minuuttia. Speech turns -ia into -ii.
Kävellä means to walk. The ending -en means 'by walking': kävellen.
